stories.headline: Paul Goldschmidt says time with Yankees prepared him for expectations Mets face
stories.summary: Paul Goldschmidt knew Mets manager Andy Green from their time together with Arizona in 2015 and was eager make the move across town from the Yankees to reunite.
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- Paul Goldschmidt knew New York Mets manager Andy Green from their time together with Arizona in 2015 and was eager make the move across town from the Yankees to reunite.

"It's an exciting team, a very talented team. I think there's really high expectations for this team," the first baseman said Wednesday after finalizing an $8 million, one-year contract with the Mets. "The expectations of this organization are to win the World Series from the outside looking in and I have no doubt that the players and coaches, front office, ownership feel that same way."

Green was Goldschmidt's third-base coach with the Diamondbacks in 2015, then left to become San Diego's manager. Green replaced Carlos Mendoza as Mets manager in June and was given a three-year contract in September.

"We always stayed in touch. I think he's really smart and he really has a game plan of how he wants to attack things," Goldschmidt said. "I remember him just being very open to continuing to learn. He didn't think he had all the answers and so, that's always very encouraging."

A seven-time All-Star who spent the past two seasons across town with the Yankees, the 39-year-old hit .252 with 18 homers, 52 RBI and a .765 OPS in 380 plate appearances over 105 games this year, then became a free agent.

As part of his Mets deal, Goldschmidt can earn an additional $2 million in performance bonuses for plate appearances: $500,000 each for 450 and 475, and $1 million for 500.

"Being with the other team in New York the last couple years, you know the expectations of this city," Goldschmidt said. "There was nothing that anyone really needed to sell me on. I knew that going in and so when they called it was exciting."

He's eager to team with Tarik Skubal, who has a pending $450 million, nine-year agreement with the Mets, a record for a pitcher.

"I got a chance to play with him on Team USA," Goldschmidt said, referring to this year's World Baseball Classic. "He was a great guy, a great leader and a competitor, and obviously an amazing pitcher."

Goldschmidt, the 2022 NL MVP with St. Louis, will likely platoon with left-handed-hitting first baseman Jared Young.

"My top concern was not: Hey, how do I go to someplace where I get the most playing time?" he said. "My concern was going to a team where it felt right."

A right-handed hitter, Goldschmidt batted .299 with 11 homers and a .967 OPS in 183 plate appearances against left-handed pitchers this year. He is a .322 career hitter versus lefties, with a 1.004 OPS.

"It's been fun to have a different perspective. It's kind of like a relief pitcher. You think you're going to come into the game in the fifth and you don't come into until the seventh," he said. "So it's like trying to find that balance of being ready so that the game doesn't sneak up."

Goldschmidt is a four-time Gold Glove winner with a .286 average, 390 home runs, 1,284 RBIs and an .877 OPS in 16 major league seasons with the Diamondbacks, Cardinals and Yankees.

"I enjoyed playing in New York. When I was a visiting player, you enjoy the adrenaline that comes with these games, with the energy that you can feel in the stadium," he said. "The No. 1 thing I would just say about this city is the high expectations of both these teams and really all the sports teams and really anything that goes on in New York."

stories.headline: Williams, Alpine fined £627k by FIA for breaching F1's cost cap
stories.summary: The FIA has announced that Williams overspent by £627,000 under F1's cost cap last year, while Williams and Alpine both committed "procedural" breaches.
stories.body:
The FIA has announced that Williams overspent by £627,000 ($821, 869) under Formula 1's cost cap last year, while Williams and Alpine both committed "procedural" breaches under the sport's financial regulations for 2025.

The two teams have accepted the findings of the FIA's Cost Cap Administration (CCA) and entered into accepted breach agreements (ABAs), by which each team acknowledges their overstep and agrees to a penalty.

Williams will face a financial penalty and a 1.5% reduction in its wind tunnel and CFD (Computational Fluid Dynamics) time next year, while Alpine will only face a financial penalty.

Williams overspent by £627,000 last year, which equates to a 0.48% breach of the 2025 budget cap.

In a statement released by the FIA, the CCA recognised the following points.

"There is no accusation or evidence that WGPE [Williams Grand Prix Engineering] sought at any time to act in bad faith, dishonestly or in a fraudulent manner, nor that it wilfully concealed any information from the Cost Cap Administration.

"The Financial Regulations are complex, and the breaches arose from an interpretation adopted by WGPE in good faith; WGPE has accepted the FIA's interpretation and the resulting breaches.

"There is no evidence that WGPE gained or sought to gain any advantage (sporting or otherwise) from the identified breaches; and the Minor Overspend Breach amounts to £627k and therefore, with 0.48% over the 2025 Cost Cap, falls at the lower end of the

Williams also issued a statement acknowledging the breach.

"Atlassian Williams F1 Team has reached an Accepted Breach Agreement with the FIA in relation to our 2025 Cost Cap submission," the team statement said.

"The FIA has determined that the team committed a minor overspend breach and an accompanying procedural breach, unintentionally exceeding the cap by £627,000 - 0.48% over the 2025 Cost Cap. The agreed outcome is a financial penalty and a 1.5% reduction in wind tunnel and CFD testing over the next 12 months.

"The breach relates to administrative costs we incurred making changes to our company structure. We believed these costs fell outside of the cap. Following discussions with the FIA, we have agreed to resolve the matter in line with their interpretation that the costs should have been in cap.

"The FIA has noted that Williams did not gain any sporting or financial advantage, and nor did we ever seek to. It has also noted that we acted cooperatively and in good faith throughout the review process.

"Integrity is central to what Williams stands for and we can now close this case and remain focused on our future.

"We have always been and will continue to be strong supporters of the Cost Cap, which naturally requires accurate policing to be effective."

Although Alpine did not overspend in 2025, its financial reporting included inaccuracies relating to marketing activities, non-F1 activities, HR activities, employee bonus costs, offsetting of costs and costs of inventories.

As with Williams, the FIA made clear that Alpine had not acted in a fraudulent manner nor sought to gain an advantage.

Alpine accepted the findings, and its financial penalty, in a statement of its own.

"BWT Alpine Formula One Team acknowledges and accepts the findings of the Cost Cap Administration (CCA) for the 2025 Reporting Period," the statement said. "The team accepts that it unknowingly committed a Procedural Breach, which is a result of inaccuracies in the Full Year Reporting Documentation for costs related to exclusions and adjustments.

"The errors and inaccuracies in the reporting were specifically related to non-sporting and operational costs which the CCA recognised didn't give the team any performance advantage, such as Marketing Activities, non-F1 Activities, HR Activities, Employee's Bonus Costs, Offsetting of Costs, and Costs of Inventories.

"The team would also like to express its thanks to both the CCA and FIA, for its diligence and understanding throughout the entire process. The Financial Regulations are still relatively new, constantly evolving and complex, with some exclusions and adjustments being open to each team's interpretation. The team acknowledges the collective efforts it needs to make across the business and recognises where improvements can be made in future."

The other nine F1 teams were found to be in compliance with the 2025 financial regulations.

F1 introduced its cost cap in 2021 to make the series more sustainable and provide a more level the playing field between the biggest teams and the sport's backmarkers.

Red Bull was found to be in breach of the very first cost cap after it emerged it had overspent by 1.6% in 2021, resulting in a $7 million fine for the team and a 10% reduction in its wind tunnel and CFD time.

stories.headline: Chiefs rule RB Kenneth Walker III (groin) out for showdown vs. Bills
stories.summary: Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III (groin) has been ruled out for Thursday's showdown against the Bills, the team announced Wednesday
stories.body:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III will not play in Thursday night's showdown against the Buffalo Bills, the team announced Wednesday.

Walker will miss his third consecutive game with a grade-two groin strain. Since the Chiefs are playing on a short week, the team is holding Walker out against the Bills to give him more time to rest. After playing the Bills, the Chiefs will face the Los Angeles Rams on the road next Thursday night.

Walker was a limited participant in Tuesday's practice, the Chiefs' lone on-field work this week.

Starting in Walker's place will be rookie running back Emmett Johnson, who has been impressive in his past four games. During that stretch, Johnson produced 491 all-purpose yards and five total touchdowns, including back-to-back 100-plus yard rushing efforts in wins over Atlanta and Arizona the last two weeks in Walker's absence.

"It's been great having an opportunity to watch Emmett do his thing because that's what he's supposed to do," offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy said Monday. "The next man should always have that mentality because we're coaching the starter to be the starter, but we're also coaching that next man to be prepared to be the man. I think Emmett has done a great job, but we also understand the value that Kenneth brings."

The Chiefs expect to have right guard Trey Smith back in the starting lineup after he missed last week's win over the Cardinals while in the NFL's concussion protocol. Right tackle Jaylon Moore, who has a right ankle injury, has also been ruled out against the Bills. Joshua Ezeudu is once again expected to step in for Moore.

stories.headline: Aleksander Barkov, Brad Marchand returning from injuries against Senators
stories.summary: Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand are about to be in the Panthers' lineup together for the first time since the title-clinching game of the 2025 Stanley Cup Final.
stories.body:
Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand are about to be in the Florida Panthers' lineup together for the first time since the title-clinching game of the 2025 Stanley Cup Final, which was more than 17 months ago.

The Panthers made the announcement Wednesday morning that both are returning from knee injuries and expected to play against the Ottawa Senators.

"They're back," the team said in a social media post.

The returns were not unexpected, though Marchand's might have come a few days before the Panthers initially anticipated. Florida made some roster adjustments this week to free up cap space needed to get both into the lineup, the clearest sign that the returns were close.

Both appeared in only two of Florida's first 24 games this season. Barkov played the first two, Marchand played the next two, and both got hurt during their second contests of the campaign. Late November was always the target for both, and they evidently hit the rehab finish line together.

Barkov missed all of last season because of ligament tears in his right knee. He played in Florida's first two games this season, both on the road, before hurting his left knee Oct. 1. Marchand made his season debut Oct. 4 then hurt his knee in a game two days later.

Both have been practicing for much of November.

Marchand, 38, is in his third season with the Panthers after playing his first 16 seasons with the rival Boston Bruins. He was traded to Florida in March 2025 and helped the Panthers win their second straight Stanley Cup that season.

Barkov, 31, is Florida's all-time leader in goals, assists and points. He was the team's leader in games played as well, but since getting hurt he has ceded that spot to Panthers defenseman Aaron Ekblad.

"It's huge," Panthers defenseman Niko Mikkola said of Barkov. "He's the face of the team, the leader and probably our most important player."

stories.headline: Newcastle owners not considering full sale, only minority deals - reports
stories.summary: Newcastle's Saudi owners are not treating the possibility of selling a minority stake in the club as the first step towards a full sale, the Press Association understands.
stories.body:
Newcastle's Saudi owners are not treating the possibility of selling a minority stake in the club as the first step towards a full sale, sources told Press Association.

The Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF), which owns a majority stake in Newcastle, is understood to have enlisted JP Morgan to examine ways to fund the building of a new stadium.

One method to achieve this could be the sale of new shares in the club, with The Athletic reporting that could equate to a new investor holding up to 25% of the club's shares and diluting the PIF's stake.

News of a willingness to consider selling a minority stake may on the surface make fans question the owners' long-term commitment, but sources close to the PIF insist it should not be interpreted that way and that work to finance a new stadium should instead be seen as a signal of the PIF's willingness to remain for the long haul.

- Raheem Sterling avoids jail for dangerous driving

- Transfer rumors, news: Manchester United's Bruno Fernandes eyed by Juventus

- Transfer rumors, news: Arsenal, Newcastle eye Inter's Pio Esposito

Any serious offer to buy the club would always be considered, sources said, because the PIF is ultimately seeking a financial return as an investment fund. However, that is absolutely not the purpose of the process the PIF is now embarking on with JP Morgan, sources told Press Association.

Earlier this year, the PIF ended its investment in the LIV Golf series, which has since collapsed into bankruptcy.

Newcastle have already announced plans for a new training complex near the city's international airport, but have not yet confirmed whether they will press ahead with building a new stadium.

Newcastle and the PIF have been contacted for comment.

NBA Trade Lab: What deals could OKC make?
The Oklahoma City Thunder are at a critical inflection point. After winning a championship in 2024, they spent most of last season as the title favorites, only to be upended by Victor Wembanyama's San Antonio Spurs in Game 7 of the Western Conference finals. Coming into the season, ESPN's Basketball Power Index (BPI) projected them to have a 28.4% chance to win the title, the highest of any team. However, several injuries have already derailed their season, leaving them in the middle of a crowded Western Conference at 10-8 and with a decision to make on which direction to take for the rest of the season.

Some people are calling for Oklahoma City to punt on the season and regroup in 2027-28. With an All-Star in Jalen Williams and an All-Defensive player in Cason Wallace out of the lineup, is it worth using valuable draft capital to attempt to salvage what could turn into a lost season? Other people are adamant that now is the time for the Thunder to make an aggressive trade, dipping into their treasure trove of draft assets so they don't squander a year of reigning back-to-back MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's prime.

The challenge for the Thunder in making a trade, however, is their growing cap sheet and current roster construction. With max extensions for their young core of Gilgeous-Alexander, Williams and Chet Holmgren on the books, they are just $3 million below the dreaded second apron. Beyond those three, the only other players on the team earning above $8 million annually are Alex Caruso and Isaiah Hartenstein, both of whom are invaluable to the Thunder's identity. This makes it difficult to include Caruso or Hartenstein in trades that would actually improve their championship hopes for this season.

The remaining 10 players on their roster are all on extremely team-friendly deals, which actually works against the Thunder for the sake of facilitating a trade. Many of these young players would field significant value across the league, but their low salaries make it tough to aggregate outgoing money to match the paycheck of a veteran who could meaningfully improve OKC.

Out of that group, Nikola Topic and Thomas Sorber might be the most logical trade candidates. They have been the two most-traded Thunder players in ESPN's NBA Trade Lab, after a series of injuries have kept them off the floor for the majority of their young careers. The Thunder recently declined to pick up Topic's $7.4 million option for next season, making him an unrestricted free agent in 2027.

Let's evaluate a couple of the top fan-created trades from our NBA Trade Lab involving these two players to see what the Thunder could realistically bring back to help them this season:

Trade No. 1: OKC adds a talented defender
Thunder get: Herb Jones

New Orleans Pelicans get: Sorber, Topic, one first-round pick

Oklahoma City led the NBA in defensive turnover Net Points in each of the previous three seasons, but it has slipped to league-average this season. The Thunder's identity hinges on creating havoc and extra possessions, and without several key stoppers, they suddenly are much less intimidating in this area.

Bringing in Jones, an all-defense-caliber wing who has always created turnovers, could help to restore their defensive edge until the return of some of their key defensive personnel. Jones might not provide much on offense, but one of Gilgeous-Alexander's superpowers is his ability to captain an elite offense even in a weak surrounding offensive context, allowing the Thunder to pack lineups full of suffocating defenders and still be competent on offense.

Trade No. 2: OKC deals for instant offense help
Thunder get: Ty Jerome and Olivier-Maxence Prosper

Memphis Grizzlies get: Sorber, Topic, two first-round picks

Jerome has been a breakout star for the Grizzlies, thriving in an expanded role as their primary creator while still maintaining his elite shotmaking, especially with his floater in the midrange. Net Points rated Jerome as one of the league's most impactful players since his 2023-24 season with the Cleveland Cavaliers, and now that he has been given a featured role on an upstart Memphis team, his talent has become clear.

Jerome holds a $9 million player option for next season, and the Grizzlies can re-sign him to only a four-year, $72 million deal with his Bird rights, which is arguably below what his contract value would be on the open market. This leaves Memphis in a difficult position with Jerome potentially headed toward unrestricted free agency in 2027. Trading him now for two young players and two first-round picks might be a better option than risking him leaving for nothing in the summer.

The challenge with this trade is the Thunder would also be limited in their ability to re-sign Jerome in the summer, given their current cap constraints and proximity to the second apron. If Jerome fits well alongside Gilgeous-Alexander and OKC decides to re-sign him long term, the team would likely need to trade one of its higher-paid foundational players to make room. -- Ben Tiemeyer

NBA Trade Lab: Dejounte Murray's trade request
After formally requesting a trade last Friday, New Orleans Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray has unsurprisingly been the player most involved in fan-created trades over the past seven days in our NBA Trade Lab.

The Spurs traded Murray to the Hawks in 2022 for a massive haul: three first-round picks (including the Hawks' pick in the upcoming 2027 draft) and one first-round pick swap. At the time, Murray was viewed as a burgeoning young star with a strong impact on both sides of the ball. In Atlanta he expanded his offensive game, but his defensive impact, as measured by Net Points, fell off a cliff. In 2024, the Hawks sent him to the Pelicans in exchange for a package that included two first-round picks and Dyson Daniels, who went on to win Most Improved Player the following season.

Now in 2026, it appears likely Murray will be on the move again, but his market is difficult to read. His impact metrics have been on the decline, and he's making over $30 million for the next two seasons after turning 30 years old. At the same time, he is undoubtedly a talented player who could certainly find a renaissance in the right situation. Let's look at some of the top fan-created trades to see what fans are thinking might be a realistic deal.

Trade No. 1: A one-for-one swap
Pelicans get: Jalen Green

Phoenix Suns get: Murray

Green and Murray are similar in many ways, so a straight-up swap could make sense for both teams. Green is a talented scorer, but he lacks consistency and doesn't offer the ancillary skills to buoy him at a constant floor of positive impact. He is also only 24, the same age as Warriors Rookie of the Year candidate Yaxel Lendeborg, so the Pelicans could see room to further develop him in their system.

For the Suns, this would be a bet on their system. They have built a menacing defensive identity over the past two seasons and often punch above their weight through effort and hustle. Bringing Murray into this system could help to revive some of the defensive aspects of his game that have faded in recent years.

Trade No. 2: New Orleans dumps Murray for picks
Pelicans get: Four second-round picks

Charlotte Hornets get: Murray

In this unusual deal, the Pelicans get no players back. It is a valid trade because of the $40 million trade exception that the Hornets received in the LaMelo Ball trade. Four second-round picks may not sound like much, but in the process the Pelicans would also open up a $32 million trade exception of their own and would completely clear Murray's money off their books without receiving any undesirable contracts in return.

The Hornets' offense has been really struggling this season, ranking last in Offensive Net Points per game, after losing their offensive engine in LaMelo Ball. Trading for Murray could inject some life into their offense, strengthening their guard play while they wait for Kon Knueppel to return from injury and Coby White to return to form after a slow start to his season.

Trade No. 3: San Antonio takes a chance
Pelicans get: De'Aaron Fox and Spurs 2029 first-round pick

San Antonio Spurs get: Murray and Herb Jones

The Pelicans here get a proven winner and veteran presence in Fox, who could help to mentor Jeremiah Fears and their other young players throughout their roster. They also receive a 2029 first-round pick to build their future draft capital.

The Spurs are rolling right now and Fox has been playing great, so this would likely be a trade they consider only if things start to go downhill a bit and they decide they want to get off Fox's contract. San Antonio might be more interested in Murray than other teams, since he played some of his best basketball there. "It was kind of sad. Playing with LeBron was amazing. There's a lot of things I learned from him. ... We all know who LeBron James is."

Shams: Duren's relationship with Pistons "has fractures"

Simmons "didn't touch a ball for a year"

During Sacramento Kings media day, guard Ben Simmons laid out the reasons he chose the Kings and why he's excited for the 2026-27 season.

"The expectations are low. I feel like that's been something on me too, so we can relate in that way," Simmons told reporters. "I think we have a chip on our shoulder."

Simmons last played in 2024-25, appearing in 51 games for the Brooklyn Nets and LA Clippers. The three-time All-Star said the time away gave him the chance to focus on "getting my body right and my mind right."

Pistons GM hasn't spoken with Duren all summer

Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons have a decision to make as the clock ticks closer to Oct. 1 -- the deadline to sign a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer.

For Duren, he can accept the five-year, $200 million contract that has been offered by Detroit or he can become the first player named All-NBA or All-Star to sign the qualifying offer. If he chooses the latter, Duren will hold veto power on any trade this season and be an unrestricted free agent next summer.

For the Pistons, weighing the risk of having an All-NBA player on a one-year contract and, more importantly, the likelihood he will depart next summer as a free agent is key.

There are eight projected teams that have significant cap space to sign Duren to a four-year, $189 million max contract.

"I can't control the different things that he does or his group does," Pistons president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon said at media day. "For me, it's control what we can and letting him know he is a big part of what we do."

Langdon also said he hasn't spoken with Duren all summer during Pistons media day. -- Bobby Marks

Mitchell: LeBron to Cavs made sense "for a lot of reasons"

At Cavaliers media day, Donovan Mitchell said that in his mind, he thought LeBron James would return to Cleveland because "for a lot of reasons it made sense."

"I didn't think Philly. I thought if he didn't come here, it'd be Golden State," Mitchell said.

After being swept in the Eastern Conference finals by the eventual champion New York Knicks then missing out on James in free agency, Cleveland kept its core intact. The Cavs signed Mitchell to a four-year, $273 million maximum extension and re-signed James Harden to a three-year, $97 million contract. Cleveland did make one major addition by acquiring Peyton Watson from the Denver Nuggets in a multiteam trade then signing the restricted free agent to a four-year, $88 million deal.

Speaking for the first time since their extensions, Mitchell and Harden both said their approaches to their new deals -- Mitchell signing as soon as he was eligible with Harden opting out to give Cleveland more flexibility to make moves -- reflected a team-first mindset.

"This is something that I want to do, and I want to win a championship," Harden said. "So, what does that look like? Making the team better, making the team whole to where we give ourselves a chance. By the way, you can have the best talented team, which I've been on before, and still not win.

"We waited, waited, waited until the front office called me, made sure that we got everything that we can get, and then we signed. We got a long way to go, but I love the direction and steps that we're taking here as a unit from top to bottom." -- Daniel Oyefusi

MacMahon: Thunder adjusting to roster changes
The departures of three championship-winning teammates doesn't yet feel like reality for Thunder superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, who kidded that he still expected Luguentz Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins to show up for Oklahoma City's team picture Monday afternoon.

"It's the business of the NBA, right?" Gilgeous-Alexander said, referring to the series of financially motivated trades. "I don't think anybody has played with all 12 guys their whole career. It sucks a little bit.

"My mind never even went to what we were going to be like on the court. It was more like the brotherhood."

As fellow OKC guard Jalen Williams added, "It's the weirdest thing ever." -- Tim MacMahon

Clippers announce Ingram has partially torn Achilles

The LA Clippers announced they found a partially torn Achilles tendon in Brandon Ingram's foot after his recent heel surgery. He will miss the start of the 2026-27 season.

Jokic: "I'm gonna sign next year"

Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokic reiterated his commitment to the franchise at Monday's media day.

"I'm gonna sign next year," Jokic said. "If they want me."

Curry said knee is ready to go for the season

Golden State Warriors superstar guard Stephen Curry addressed the media Monday in offering positive updates on his injured knee.

"Knee's feeling great. Ready to go. No issues," Curry said. "I feel a lot stronger and understanding of what I'm dealing with."

Curry did acknowledge a "management element" but said there are currently no restrictions.

Nuggets confident in Jokic's future with franchise

Members of the Denver Nuggets' front office, general manager Jon Wallace and executive vice president of basketball Ben Tenzer addressed the media on Monday and answered questions regarding Nikola Jokic's future with the franchise. The three-time MVP didn't sign an extension this offseason.

"We feel very comfortable with the relation and trust there," Tenzer said. "We have no concerns."

LeBron: I wanted to finish my career with the Knicks
New Philadelphia 76er LeBron James said his decision came down to five teams this offseason and that he envisioned going to the New York Knicks before they won the 2026 title.

"I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James told ESPN on Monday during the 76ers' media day. "One of the best places I've ever played.

"I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it."

James and the 76ers will play the Knicks at the Garden on opening night, Oct. 20.

No update on Gary Trent Jr. investigation

Milwaukee Bucks governor Wes Edens did not provide an update on the league investigation into Gary Trent Jr.'s contract.

"I don't have any update," Edens said. "We're working with the league and fully cooperating with them. But I don't have any insight beyond that."

The NBA is looking into a potential cap-circumvention violation by the Bucks around Trent's deal this offseason.

Cronin: Blazers have "belief" in Ja Morant
Portland Trail Blazers' general manager Joe Cronin addressed why the franchise decided to trade for Ja Morant this offseason during Portland's media day on Monday.

"Just straight belief in Ja," Cronin said. "Our view of Ja as still a very high-level player.

"I'm sure there will be questions about fit, but we're very focused on talent."

Cronin also said veteran guard Jrue Holiday could play some minutes on the wing for Portland this season, while adding that Holiday and veteran guard Damian Lillard will have a positive influence on Morant.

Kerr: Rookie Lendeborg going to "play a ton"

Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr said during Monday's media day that he expects rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to "play a ton" this season.

"He's clearly going to play a ton," Kerr said. "He gives us the size and the versatility that we need.

"Whether he's a starter or coming off the bench, that will be determined the next couple of weeks."

Lendeborg was the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft and averaged 15.1 points per game at Michigan last season.

Embiid: 'Extremely excited' about this year's team
Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said Monday that he feels like the team finally has the right mix of players, after an offseason in which the franchise traded for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join the young guard tandem of VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey.

"It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe," he said. "I'm extremely excited about this team because we have the right mix of veteran leadership and younger guys. We might have some ups and downs, but we're gonna get there."

Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss
After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season.

"I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said.

Harper addresses role for coming season
After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season.

"Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in."

First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform
New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team:

"Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language."

LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win.

"Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything"

Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward
In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings.

"I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors."

Haliburton: I am 100% healthy
Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season.

"I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year."

Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors
Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team.
In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors.

Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction
After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room.

"We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room."

"I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control."

And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done."

Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp
After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday.

Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft.

Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp
Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday.

Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said.

Sept. 26

Bulls trade Dillingham to Hornets for Hield, cash
The Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets agreed to a trade sending Rob Dillingham to Charlotte for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Saturday.

2026 NBA offseason trade grades

Sept. 25

What's next for Curry and the Warriors?
Stephen Curry's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings.

The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in position to have extra spending power next summer.

By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase its projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for $3 million.

For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. They will be free agents next summer.

Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski. The 2023 first-round pick is eligible until Oct. 19 to extend his contract. -- Bobby Marks

Grading the Curry deal: Why Warriors don't get an A

Hornets star Knueppel sidelined by hamstring injury
The Charlotte Hornets announced that Kon Knueppel will be out for at least the entire preseason because of a left hamstring injury.

James: Maxey, Embiid were factors in joining 76ers
LeBron James said his longstanding friendship with All-Star Tyrese Maxey and a desire to help Joel Embiid win his first NBA title played significant roles in his decision to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers in July.

"[Embiid has] done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into the process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump."

Grizzlies waive Russell
The Memphis Grizzlies have waived D'Angelo Russell, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Russell has made one All-Star team during his career and was selected No. 2 in the 2015 NBA draft.

stories.headline: Is your team out of the MLS playoffs? Adopt these chaos clubs as your 2nd side
stories.summary: Your favorite team isn't going to win MLS Cup, so we dug into our catalog of statistics to pinpoint three chaos clubs to follow for the postseason.
stories.body:
Let's be honest: Your favorite team isn't going to win MLS Cup this season.

Out of 30 clubs, 16 qualified for the ongoing Round 1 series, and of those playoff invitees, only one will lift the trophy next month. The odds aren't in your favor, so what's a fan to do when considering other teams to follow? And more importantly: What if you just want to be entertained when looking at the rest of the bracket?

We've got you covered. Here at ESPN, we've leaned into MLS After Dark vibes and dug into our detailed catalog of season-wide statistics to pinpoint three chaos clubs to follow during the playoffs. This isn't a list of title favorites, instead it's teams that willingly -- or in some cases, unwillingly -- showcase last-minute plot twists, controversy and disorganized performances.

It can all be messy and uncontrolled, but that's part of the beauty of an unpredictable league like MLS.

Ready to embrace some chaos? Let's dive in.

Late drama and stoppage-time fireworks: FC Cincinnati

Game-winning and game-tying goals: Ranked 1st

Stoppage-time goals: Ranked 1st

Goals scored minutes 76-90: Ranked 1st

Goals scored against minutes 76-90: Ranked 6th (tied)

Comeback wins: Ranked 4th (tied)

Points dropped from winning positions: Ranked 3rd

Stoppage-time madness, conceding and allowing late goals, dropping plenty of points but also capable of comebacks -- what more could you want?

Unsurprisingly, this constant push and pull for head coach Pat Noonan and his roster has led to Cincinnati narrowly sneaking into the playoffs after finishing ninth in the Eastern Conference. In the Wild Card play-in against Orlando City SC last week, we saw Cincinnati's season distilled into one match after conceding an early goal and then scoring three goals themselves, including one in the 85th minute to secure the 3-1 victory.

Regardless of what happens as the obvious underdogs against the Supporters' Shield-winning Nashville SC in the remainder of the series that FCC leads 1-0, attacking names such as Evander and Kévin Denkey will make things interesting with their exploits in the final third.

Evander himself was recently blunt about how inconsistent things have looked in 2026, but also confident that they could still make noise in the playoffs.

"There's been a lot of pressure on us throughout the whole season because, to be honest, we haven't had a good season," the Brazilian said after defeating Orlando. "And this is the time to change. I just told the boys to come out and enjoy the night. I think we need to enjoy the next upcoming games and try to save the season ... if we play like we played tonight, we can make it to the final."

Masters of the dark arts: Philadelphia Union
Fouls committed: Ranked 1st

Direct red cards: Ranked 4th (tied)

Yellow cards: Ranked 8th (tied)

Penalties won: Ranked 2nd (tied)

Penalties conceded: Ranked 13th (tied)

VAR events: Ranked 3rd (tied)

Looking for a bit of grit, penalties in favor, and shirt-pulling when the referee isn't looking? The Union are a perfect club for the dark arts when it comes to fans who are eager to watch a scrappy side that pushes the envelope.

And by scrappy, this isn't necessarily what someone might call a "dirty" style of play. It's high pressing, it's galvanized by a youthful core that includes the likes of up-and-coming U.S. men's national team players such as Cavan Sullivan and Neil Pierre, and it's been effective with a strong finish to the second half of the regular season.

What's interesting to note is that despite leading the league in fouls committed, they're eighth in yellow cards, pointing to the squad being more clever with their stoppages in play, as opposed to just recklessly diving into challenges and duels. In the face of that lengthy list of fouls, they're also only ranked at 13th when it comes to conceding penalties against them.

For comparison, Philadelphia has given up five penalties against this season, which is fewer than four other playoff teams and half of the league-leading total.

Those VAR situations are still ever-present, though, creating some edge-of-your seat moments in 2026.

At the very least, the Union are worth watching when it comes to Sullivan, their teenage star. Bound for Manchester City once he turns 18, the attacking midfielder has been effective with 14 goal contributions in his past 14 appearances.

No clean sheet goalfest: Inter Miami CF

Goals scored: Ranked 1st

Total goals scored and against: Ranked 3rd

Total xG for and against: Ranked 3rd

xG: Ranked 3rd

Shots on goal: Ranked 2nd

Even with Lionel Messi, things can still be messy for Miami.

In order to find the last time the club earned a scoreless draw in all competitions, you would have to go back to March 14, when they drew (without their Argentine star) away from home against Charlotte FC. There was only one other 0-0 tie all season: three days before that in Nashville.

Clearly, if you're only looking for goals, Miami is the answer and Messi is the catalyst for the club's attacking efforts. The World Cup winner finished the regular season with an astounding tally of 26 goals and 16 assists across 32 appearances, meaning that if you're tuning in, you'll likely see him finding the back of the net or being involved in the chance creation of a game-changing moment.

And yet there's a reason why they finished third in the Supporters' Shield table.

Their defense has been highly questionable with the amount of goals that they've allowed. In fact, no team within the top 13 of that Supporters' Shield table has allowed more goals (59) than Miami.

Messi and friends will create plenty of opportunities in the final third, but can they shut out their opponents? That's an entirely different conversation and a reason to follow along with this now-deemed chaos club.

stories.headline: Sparks forward Cameron Brink, Ben Felter wed at Stanford
stories.summary: The couple met in 2021 and was engaged in 2024 before marrying at their alma mater's Memorial Church.
stories.body:
Cameron Brink and Ben Felter have officially tied the knot after holding a ceremony on Nov. 14 at their alma mater Stanford's Memorial Church.

According to a report Tuesday from Vogue Magazine, which shared behind-the-scenes details and images, the Los Angeles Sparks forward had four bridal looks, including a custom dress from bridal designer Danielle Frankel for the ceremony, and another for the reception.

Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha, were among those in attendance. Curry and Brink are godsiblings as their fathers were teammates at Virginia Tech, and their mothers were roommates on campus.

The reception was at Ritz-Carlton, Half Moon Bay, while vows were exchanged at Memorial Church, one of the earliest interdenominational churches in the West. The waiting list to get married there can be up to four years, but alumni receive a shorter period, according to Vogue. The couple told the magazine that they always knew they wanted to wed there.

"Walking past the ornate mosaics on my way to class was always the best part of my day," Brink said.

Brink and Felter met at Stanford in the fall of 2020. The two began dating in March 2021 after Felter sent Brink an email in which he included his phone number. Felter, who rowed at Stanford, proposed to Brink in Paris in September 2024.

The No. 2 pick in the 2024 WNBA draft, Brink averaged a career-high 9.5 points plus five rebounds and 1.8 blocks for Los Angeles in the 2026 season.

stories.headline: Navajo Stirling belts another former champ, moves up in rankings
stories.summary: Here's a look at every weight class to determine the best of the best in UFC, PFL and beyond.
stories.body:
If you've ever worn a UFC light heavyweight championship belt, watch out for Navajo Stirling.

His two most recent victories have come against former 205-pound champions, both knockouts. After a first-round finish of Jan Blachowicz in August, the New Zealander knocked out Jiří Procházka in Saturday's UFC Fight Night main event in Qatar.

As a result, Stirling leapfrogs Procházka in the ESPN divisional rankings, rising to No. 3 at light heavyweight. After his fourth straight knockout overall, Stirling (12-0) is right behind the division's champion, Carlos Ulberg, Stirling's training partner at City Kickboxing in Auckland. The No. 1 ranking belongs to former champion Magomed Ankalaev, who called out Stirling after Saturday's fight.

The weekend's UFC fights also led to changes in the featherweight and men's flyweight top 10s. Aljamain Sterling lost a 145-pound fight to Kevin Vallejos and drops four spots to No. 7, right below Vallejos. At 125 pounds, Kyoji Horiguchi moves up one position to No. 6 after beating Asu Almabayev, who remains 10th.

stories.headline: Price tag for Tassie's new AFL stadium goes up, again
stories.summary: The estimated cost of a new 23,000-seat waterfront venue, set to eventually become the home of the Tasmania Devils, has risen again.
stories.body:
Tasmania's new AFL stadium has suffered another cost blowout, causing the premier to break a promise to cap the state's spend as critics fear the end price will be far higher.

The cost estimate for the 23,000-seat roofed venue at Macquarie Point in Hobart has increased from $1.13 billion to $1.23 billion.

On top of the figure is $132 million for broader precinct infrastructure, project delivery costs of $183 million and unspecified contingencies, taking the total to $1.54 billion.

Premier Jeremy Rockliff previously pledged to cap Tasmania's contribution to the build at $875 million as part of a deal to get the project through parliament.

But he conceded on Tuesday the state would have to cover the slated $100 million increase via extra borrowings.

"The previous cost estimate, which we announced ... some 14 months ago, there's been a lot of water under the bridge since that point," Mr Rockliff said.

The premier confirmed the project wouldn't head back to parliament for the approval of the necessary extra funding, despite previous assurances it would.

The latest estimate reflects increases in the cost of construction, sustained high oil and materials prices, higher labour costs and its complexity, the state government said.

The stadium is expected to be ready for the 2031 AFL season and was a condition of the Tasmania Devils being granted a licence to enter into the national competition in 2028.

It initially had a price tag of $715 million.

Mr Rockliff said the state had reached out to the federal government and AFL for extra money on top of their $240 million and $15 million contributions.

Anti-stadium group Our Place Hobart said the new cost estimate failed to take into account other factors, including the interest bill and the exact cost of contingencies.

Greens leader Rosalie Woodruff described the ongoing cost increases as a deep betrayal of Tasmanians.

"Who knows where the final price for the stadium will end up?" she said.

"What we do know is there's been now a fifth major cost blowout and there's not yet a contract price locked in for this massive project."

Federal independent MP Andrew Wilkie fears the stadium will end up costing $2 billion.

"Once you add the cost of the debt over a decade, the total cost to the Tasmanian taxpayer is closer to $3.5 billion," he said.

Devils chief executive Brendon Gale said the question of any additional funding from the AFL was a matter for the sport's governing body.

"The politicians can politic. We'll get on with building our club," he said.

"People have their views and are entitled to them. But based on my experience, people never look back. These types of projects transform cities and states."

The release of updated costs came ahead of schedule after the government bowed to political pressure to make the figures public before the end of the parliamentary year.

In mid-October, BESIX Watpac was announced as the preferred builder. A final contract is set to be signed by the end of 2026.

BESIX Watpac recently built a 30,000-seat roofed stadium in Christchurch in New Zealand which cost about $540 million.

Mr Rockliff said the final contract price for the Hobart stadium was unlikely to differ from the $1.23 billion estimate.

The stadium has been deeply divisive in Tasmania amid rising state debt, a stretched health system and other under-pressure services.

The AFL and federal government have been contacted for comment.

stories.headline: 'Can't judge them': who Papenhuyzen wants at the Storm
stories.summary: Ex-Melbourne star Ryan Papenhuyzen has made some big calls on who should be the next Storm coach and the one to keep from Cameron Munster and Harry Grant.
stories.body:
Ryan Papenhuyzen empathises with Cameron Munster but believes Melbourne must prioritise keeping Harry Grant if the NRL powerhouse can't hold on to both superstars.

Munster on Tuesday rejected an offer from the Storm believed to be for one year with the option of another season, labelling the terms "disappointing".

The Storm are also fighting to keep Grant, and Papenhuyzen was unequivocal when asked on Wednesday who the club should target if salary-cap pressures meant only one of the newly crowned Australian World Cup winners could stay.

"I went through something similar as Munster where I thought the club had low-balled me," the happily retired 2020 premiership-winning hero told AAP.

"But having my time out of the game now, they've got their reasons for offering those certain amounts and it might not be enough (for Munster).

"Penrith have done it for years and years. They get to a point where they can't hold their players and they've got a price for their players.

"So I understand Munster's perspective. He wants to earn as much as he can in his career and he wants to win a premiership, so that probably limits his opportunities.

"If a club's got money and they're in a premiership window, it's probably a good chance he'll go to that club."

At 28, skipper Grant is four years younger than Munster and more important long-term to the Storm, Papenhuyzen believes.

"Harry's done a brilliant job in terms of leadership," the ex-Clive Churchill Medallist turned caddy said after playing in the Australian PGA Championship pro-am in Sydney.

"The amount of care he has for everyone in that group and the way he thinks about the game, I feel really sorry for him over the last 12 months (when Melbourne missed the finals) because he's always trying to find new ideas to bring everyone.

"He's a great leader for that club going forward. I'd hate to see him go because he's a player you want to build a club around and I guess Munster is towards the back end of his career.

"He had a great World Cup, but World Cups are different to NRL seasons. You've got to lock in for a month with that, and an NRL season's a long time."

Pressed on who he'd keep as a priority, Papenhuyzen said: "Harry's probably the one leadership-wise. Just his qualities are really admirable.

"You know what Munster brings to the game. He gives you confidence standing next to him, knowing what he's going do, but I just think Harry ..."

With coach Craig Bellamy confirming he is moving on at the end of 2027, Papenhuyzen also suspects Grant might be a better for the Storm's new mentor, whomever that may be.

"Harry's really respected and in terms of trying to keep the culture, he's very open-minded too," the BMW golf correspondent said.

"He's open to new ideas, whereas Munster is very much like Bellamy - he's sort of got his way and it's worked for him for so long.

"Whatever they both decide to do, you can't judge them. It's never a right or wrong decision."

Papenhuyzen believes it would be "awesome" if Billy Slater succeeded Bellamy, but suspects "life is too good" for the Storm legend to be a head NRL coach.

"I love Jyles. If he went back there, I'd be awfully encouraged of how well they're going to go. They'd probably be my two."

But Papenhuyzen, also open to helping out the new coach, nominated Bellamy's son Aaron as a left-field option.

"Aaron's awesome with people," he said.

"He's awesome with the wider playing group and he understands that Craig sometimes pushes the boundaries. Aaron's a bit more like Wendy - Craig's, Craig's wife.

"They're both a bit more more gentle, so you've got that loving, nurturing side and potentially (he could do the job).

"I do know you just need people around you. We'd be silly to say the coach controls everything."

stories.headline: Fantasy baseball reactions to MLB offseason trades, signings
stories.summary: Track all the latest MLB free agency and trade news with fantasy baseball analysis from Tristan H. Cockcroft and Eric Karabell.
stories.byline: Tristan H. Cockcroft and Eric Karabell
stories.body:
Tracking the offseason MLB trades and signings with fantasy baseball implications for the upcoming season, Eric Karabell and Tristan H. Cockcroft will analyze and provide an outlook for all of the key players involved.

Players were allowed to sign with new teams beginning Nov. 2, although typically things don't really start to heat up until the league's annual winter meetings. This year's meetings are scheduled to take place in San Diego from Dec. 7-9. However, with the current collective bargaining agreement expiring Dec. 1, players and teams alike might end up waiting until after the dust settles on negotiations and a potential lockout before inking any new deals.

In any event, as any contracts are signed or trades get agreed to, this is the place to find all of the fantasy fallout of those deals. Be sure to check back throughout the hot stove season for updates.

Latest updates include the Kansas City Royals signing Alec Bohm, the Toronto Blue Jays signing Japanese star Kaima Taira, the Chicago Cubs signing both Trevor Rogers and Teruaki Sato and Freddy Peralta signing with the Baltimore Orioles.

Below, you will find a list of some of the top free agents at each position. Players labeled with a (Q) received a qualifying offer from their current team and had until Nov. 17 to accept it or decline and become a free agent. Players coming from Japan/Korea who were posted by their current team have a Dec. 1 deadline to reach a deal with an MLB club to play in the United States in 2027.

Note: Not every transaction warrants the attention of fantasy managers, but for those signings and trades that do merit analysis, you'll find them listed below. Players will be separated by position and then listed in chronological order of the move within each positional grouping, with the latest news coming first. Also included are links to any standalone analysis stories and/or videos regarding major free agent signings and trades. Players who end up re-signing with their previous team will not always be included.

Catcher
Some free agents: Carson Kelly, Kyle Higashioka, Gary Sanchez, James McCann, Travis d'Arnaud, Austin Hedges

First base
Paul Goldschmidt signs with Mets

Goldschmidt, 39, hit only .252 over 380 PA with the Yankees last season -- but how he did so explains why the Mets coveted him. Goldschmidt hit .299/.393/.573 with 11 home runs versus left-handed pitching, one year after posting a .336/.411/.570 line. He has not enjoyed recent success against right-handed pitching. The Mets figure to platoon Goldschmidt, perhaps with lefty-hitting Jared Young. While that should be productive for the team, it isn't so great for fantasy managers.

Goldschmidt finished outside the top 50 first basemen in 2026 scoring. Roster him in daily formats, when you can take advantage of knowing exactly when he will be in the lineup. Fade him in standard leagues. -- Karabell (11/23)

Jake Bauers signs with Red Sox
Bauers, 31, comes off the best season of his journeyman career, posting an .873 OPS with 26 homers and 86 RBIs for the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers. He admits that he considered retirement as recently as two years ago, but he stuck around for the health benefits. Good timing. Bauers gets a four-year deal with the Red Sox, where he and right-handed-hitting Willson Contreras should make for a formidable 1-2 punch in the middle of the lineup, while sharing 1B/DH duties.

While Bauers was a top-40 hitter in points formats and roto/categories leagues last season, fantasy managers probably shouldn't expect the same kind of production moving forward, even as he performs half the time at hitter-friendly Fenway Park. Bauers had never hit more than 12 home runs in any prior season and, even now, he remains a career .223 hitter with a 2.0 career WAR.

Maybe the solid 16.3% walk rate and .218 ISO will continue, but preliminary results in NFBC drafts have Bauers going just inside the top 150. Perhaps he gets a bump for heading to Boston, but likely only a modest one. -- Karabell (11/13)

Other free agents: Josh Bell, Ryan Mountcastle, Nathaniel Lowe, Ty France

Second base

Some free agents: Gleyber Torres, Jeff McNeil, Luis Arraez, Jazz Chisholm Jr., Jonathan India, Gavin Lux, Brandon Lowe (Q)

Shortstop
Ha-Seong Kim signs with Tigers
Kim couldn't have had a much worse 2026, from his appearing in only 51 games (primarily due to issues with a finger he injured when he slipped on a sheet of ice in his native Korea in January) to his tying for the third-lowest OPS+ (2) of any player with at least as many as his 147 plate appearances during the divisional era.

The Tigers might have designs on his being their everyday shortstop, but he's more likely to be yet another infielder they can shuffle around -- good news for you Kevin McGonigle keeper/dynasty managers, as it heightens the chances McGonigle will again earn dual qualification at shortstop and third base.

Kim is only a low-end SB option for deep mixed and NL-only rotisserie leagues, barring an absolutely standout spring. -- Cockcroft (11/24)

Other free agents: J.P. Crawford, Mauricio Dubon, Isiah Kiner-Falefa, Amed Rosario

Third base
Alec Bohm signs with Royals
Bohm, 30, who attended college at Wichita State in Kansas, heads closer to home after a polarizing seven-season run with the Phillies. Bohm finished runner-up for the 2020 NL Rookie of the Year award, made the 2024 All-Star team and knocked in 97 runs in consecutive seasons, before adding 88 more this past season. Miscast as a power hitter despite his 6-foot-5 frame, Bohm averaged only 14 HRs during the past five seasons in 596 PA, but he piled on RBIs because nearly half his career plate appearances came in the Nos. 4 and 5 lineup spots. Both should continue -- the RBI chances and lineup placement -- in Kansas City.

The Royals coveted a right-handed bat for the middle of their lineup. Bohm, replacing the traded Maikel Garcia at third base, should bat fourth/fifth most of the time, just like he did in Philadelphia. He should knock in runs, just like he did in Philly, because SS Bobby Witt Jr. and others will be on base. Contact-oriented corner infielders are rare in this era. Even so, only 14 third basemen scored more fantasy points in 2026. Bohm has a low strikeout rate, and he performs better versus left-handed pitching, though the change in home ballparks certainly won't help.

Defensively, um, while he made improvement at third base, it's not good news. Fantasy managers generally don't want to know unless it costs the player his starting role -- and that won't be an issue here. Let's just say Kansas City's contact pitchers (like Michael Wacha) will not be pleased by swapping out Gold Glover Garcia for Bohm at the hot corner. -- Karabell 11/25

Teruaki Sato signs with Cubs

Sato, 27 and the defending Nippon Central League Triple Crown winner, reminds many of another left-handed hitting Japanese slugger who came to the United States. Chicago White Sox 1B Munetaka Murakami, who, in his first MLB season, launched 35 home runs with a 16.6% walk rate, albeit with a .207 batting average and 35.4% strikeout rate. Sato is viewed as a better athlete, but expected to offer a similar offensive profile in the "three true outcomes" department, with power, walks and strikeouts.

This profile has value in fantasy, but Murakami averaged only 2.1 ESPN fantasy points per game, outside the top 100 hitters. He was the No. 127 hitter on the Player Rater, even though only nine hitters slugged more home runs. Should potential Sato investors expect better numbers than Murakami's debut? Sato may boast better plate discipline and a better likelihood to adjust his approach, perhaps trading some power for better contact. Fangraphs projects a .247 batting average and 30 home runs. While Murakami is not among ESPN's initial top 200 for points formats, Sato should earn a better ranking, though not among the top 100.

Though Sato is likely ticketed for an outfield corner with the Cubs, he will be eligible at third base only in fantasy drafts based on his games played in Japan in 2026. He can earn additional eligibility with 10 games played at another position in 2027. -- Karabell (11/24)

Royce Lewis traded to Dodgers
Lewis, 27 and a former first-round pick of the Twins in 2017, has long been ticketed for slugging stardom, but his road to becoming one of the premier, power-hitting third basemen has been bumpy. Lewis hit 15 home runs and knocked in 52 over 58 games and 239 PA during his breakout 2023 campaign, with a .920 OPS. Injuries have derailed him since, as Lewis has neither reached 20 home runs in a season nor approached a .800 OPS.

At least Lewis managed to stay healthy enough to reach 500 PA for the first time in 2026, though he struck out in 25.5% of his PA with a career-low 71.9% contact rate. Can the Los Angeles Dodgers get him consistently productive and keep him on the field? The Minnesota Twins clearly could not. Eligible at first base and third base, perhaps the Dodgers view Lewis as a utility option and lefty killer, but if he doesn't hit, it doesn't matter. Bump Lewis up your draft sheets a bit because of this trade, but he remains more of a late-round sleeper than a sure thing. -- Karabell 11/20

Maikel Garcia traded to Mariners

Garcia, 26, suffered through a rough 2026 season, missing months with hamstring and hand injuries, and slugging only .381 during his 82 games and 344 PA. Not that Garcia is a renowned power hitter, but he delivered 16 home runs among his 60 extra-base hits in a breakout 2025, along with 23 stolen bases, after stealing 37 bases in 2024. Garcia missed only seven games during 2024-25, so volume played a role when he finished 18th among hitters in 2025 fantasy points.

A 2025 Gold Glove winner, Garcia is one of the better defensive third basemen in baseball, and he should solidify the position for Seattle. However, while we don't know for sure where he will hit in his new lineup -- and leaving one hitter-challenging home ballpark in Kansas City for another does not help him -- it figures to be near the bottom half, which caps his fantasy upside. Expect Garcia to bounce back to some degree offensively, with his early ESPN 2027 points ranking featuring him positively as the No. 10 3B and just outside the top 100. -- Karabell (11/18)

Other free agents: Eugenio Suarez, Edmundo Sosa, Yoan Moncada, Si Hwan Roh (posted)

Outfield

Some free agents: George Springer, Trent Grisham, Ian Happ, Seiya Suzuki (Q), Randy Arozarena, Taylor Ward, Daulton Varsho, Adolis Garcia, Luis Robert Jr., Randal Grichuk, Myles Straw, Lane Thomas

Designated hitter

Some free agents: Joc Pederson, Dominic Smith

Starting pitcher
Toronto Blue Jays sign SP Kaima Taira
Having missed out on their top free-agent pitching prize, Tarik Skubal, the Blue Jays moved quickly to sign Taira, who by many accounts had the second-best raw stuff of any pitcher on this winter's market, to a five-year, $80 million contract. Taira spent seven of his first eight seasons in Japan as a reliever but transitioned beautifully to a starting pitching role in 2026, posting a Nippon Professional Baseball-leading 1.36 ERA across 22 starts and one relief appearance. Prior to that, he had posted sub-2 ERAs in each of his prior five seasons working out of the bullpen (2020-22, '24-25), 31 saves in 2025, as well as a 2.40 ERA in 23 starts while pitching out of the rotation in 2023.

That's a remarkable level of success for a pitcher who stands just 5-foot-8. Marcus Stroman is the only MLB pitcher this century who stood that height or shorter to have made as many as 10 starts. Taira's extension -- measuring the distance from the pitching rubber that the pitcher releases the baseball -- is regarded as elite, however, and to a point where he'd likely rank in the upper quarter in U.S. play in that department. Between that and his six -- and, by some accounts, as many as eight -- pitches in his repertoire, he counters the height question with a great deal of upside. Taira's command of his pitch mix is considered elite, and generally ground ball-generating, so even with some anticipated regression to his strikeout rate he might well deliver numbers that place among the top 40 pitchers in fantasy baseball.

We'll see how swiftly and smoothly Taira adapts to U.S. play, which despite becoming less demanding upon starting pitchers in the post-COVID era, still has a lengthier and more physically taxing schedule. Questions about whether he's more suited for relief than rotation work are valid, and the primary obstacle towards him earning that potential top-40 starter ranking. By signing in Toronto, where he's more likely to have the team's patience with his adapting to the rotation, Saito will earn a ranking around No. 75 at the position, in the Joey Cantillo/Trey Yesavage/Eduardo Rodriguez range. -- Cockcroft (11/24)

Freddy Peralta signs with Orioles
Peralta, 30, ended the 2026 season with a bloated 4.42 ERA and 1.33 WHIP, but those numbers hardly tell the story. The longtime Brewers ace who struck out 200 hitters during three consecutive seasons started the 2026 season with the Mets after an offseason trade, and things went poorly right away. Then, months later, the Mets traded Peralta to the Rays and, voila, all was well again!

With his mechanics tweaked and his approach refined (more changeups, fewer sliders), Peralta posted a 3.25 ERA and 1.01 WHIP during 10 Rays starts, albeit with a lower strikeout rate than typical, but at least he was good. Then he thrived in the postseason, winning ALCS MVP honors. That is what fantasy managers expect. Peralta may not be a top 20 starting pitcher for fantasy, but he should be close. Peralta ranks among the top 100 players for points and roto formats. -- Karabell (11/24)

Trevor Rogers signs with Cubs
Rogers, 29, was never going to match his incredible 2025 season, when he posted a 1.81 ERA and 0.90 WHIP during 18 starts, but his 2026 campaign (4.03, 1.18) may have still exceeded some expectations. After all, the 6-foot-5 left-hander posted a 4.92 ERA and 1.58 WHIP for the Marlins and Orioles in 2024. The 2017 first-round pick dealt with injuries, control issues and inconsistency for much of his career, among other things. Then, suddenly, he was a star, even for half a season.

Rogers probably isn't a star. The Cubs get a guy who made 30 starts (for the first time) and did his best work in the second half, with a 3.52 ERA and 1.04 WHIP, whiffing 27% of hitters. That's good, reliable work, and Rogers was among the top 40 starting pitchers in ESPN fantasy points. Can the Cubs and fantasy managers get that version in 2027? That seems reasonable. Rogers isn't an ace, but worthy of being among the top 40 starters in drafts. There is nothing wrong with that. -- Karabell (11/24)

Tarik Skubal signs with Mets

Two winters ago, the New York Mets opened their wallet to get their offensive centerpiece, Juan Soto. On Sunday, the Mets did the same to get a centerpiece for their rotation, and for a similarly record-setting deal, signing Tarik Skubal to a nine-year, $450 million contract.

Fortunately for us in fantasy, we won't need to spend as much as the Mets did to add Skubal to our rosters, but it's a good landing spot for the lefty. He'll call one of the more pitching-leaning ballparks in Citi Field his home through 2036. -- Cockcroft (11/23)

For a more in-depth look at the fantasy impact of Skubal's signing, click here.

Luis Castillo and Davis Martin traded to Rockies
What happens when the league's worst non-Rockies or Athletics pitcher (minimum 130 innings) comes to Coors Field? We're about to find out. Castillo entered 2026 riding a four-year streak with at least 350 fantasy points, 160 strikeouts and a sub-1.20 WHIP. However, a progressive drop in his velocity and a rise in his fly ball rate during that time caused him to unravel last year, first for the Seattle Mariners and then catastrophically so following his midseason trade to the Chicago White Sox. Castillo's year ended with a shoulder injury, so in addition to the Coors factor, he enters 2027 facing many questions.

Martin, meanwhile, was the far superior fantasy pitcher between these two -- by almost two times in terms of point production (242-127). Martin, though, ended 2026 on a similarly sour note. He had a 9-2 record and 2.41 ERA through his first 13 starts, but went 0-8 with a 5.72 ERA thereafter. He dealt with a calf issue, a blister and concerns that he might be tipping pitches, ultimately making only a mop-up appearance during Chicago's playoff run.

Martin was nevertheless the piece the Rockies wanted in order to agree to absorb Castillo's remaining contract. Both will probably eat innings for a Rockies rotation always in need of depth. Either could be a "matchup candidate" in road games, if they seem to have righted the ship during spring training -- which is why a lockout-influenced, shortened preseason would be detrimental to both. Still, neither pitcher is a draft-day option, given their new team. -- Cockcroft (11/20)

Twins sign Sonny Gray
Gray, now 37 years old, returns to Minnesota after a three-year detour through St. Louis and Boston. He has enjoyed a bit of a career rebirth later in his career, averaging 385.8 fantasy points over the past four seasons, and never deviating by more than 25 points in either direction in any individual year. Gray's consistency is a valuable thing in fantasy leagues, particularly points-based scoring, where his good ratios and solid innings totals are most advantageous.

That said, a two-year pattern of declining average fastball velocity and strikeout rates raises concerns that regression might hit him harder than a typical frontline starter, if not in 2027 then perhaps if he doesn't opt out and continues into his 39-year-old campaign in 2028. I've got Gray ranked amongst my top 25 fantasy starting pitchers, and within the top 75 overall, and I'd expect he will (and should) generally be drafted in that range.

Gray's acquisition, however, gives the Twins at least nine viable rotation candidates, creating a logjam of popular deep-mixed/AL-only names like Mick Abel, Zebby Matthews, Connor Prielipp for fourth/fifth starter spots. Perhaps a trade is forthcoming, preferably for some hitting to bolster the lineup and give Gray more run support, but otherwise this is a spring battle that'll be high on the list of those to watch. Only Gray, Joe Ryan, Taj Bradley and Pablo Lopez would figure to be locks. -- Cockcroft (11/18)

Bryce Miller traded to Royals
Miller, 28, emerged as a standout fantasy option for the Seattle Mariners in 2024, winning 12 games and posting a 2.94 ERA and 0.98 WHIP. Injuries and inconsistency have plagued the right-hander since then, as Miller won only eight of 39 starts in 2025-26 with a 4.82 ERA and 1.26 WHIP while permitting 38 home runs. Elbow woes ruined his 2025 campaign, and he missed the first six weeks of 2026 with an oblique injury.

Still, when Miller is healthy, he can be effective. He posted a 2.18 ERA and 0.83 WHIP prior to the 2026 All-Star break before a rough second half (and myriad home runs) ruined things. Moving from one pitcher's park in Seattle to another in Kansas City shouldn't be a factor, but at least Miller should be guaranteed a rotation spot, which was in question in Seattle. Miller is certainly a sleeper candidate to regain his place among the top 30 starting pitchers in fantasy, but ESPN's preliminary points ranking features Miller well outside the top 50 starting pitchers. -- Karabell (11/18)

Dustin May signs with White Sox

May, 29, made 31 mostly league-average starts for the Cardinals and eventual champion Brewers this season -- many of them quite abbreviated. In fact, he ended up averaging fewer than four innings over his 10 Brewers starts and he did not qualify for the ERA title. The desperate White Sox figure to allow May to go deeper into games, but that comes at a cost, since he posted a 4.70 ERA and a 1.32 WHIP with only 0.4 bWAR last season.

Hey, at least May stayed healthy, which is a feat for him. Plus, he was a bit unlucky, as his 3.54 FIP indicates. However, that doesn't mean May warrants inclusion in ESPN standard drafts, with a preliminary points-league rank outside the top 75 starting pitchers. -- Karabell (11/18)

Other free agents: Michael King, Robbie Ray, Brandon Woodruff, Zac Gallen, Shota Imanaga, Kevin Gausman, Chris Bassitt, Jack Flaherty, Jameson Taillon, Max Scherzer, Clay Holmes, Matthew Boyd, Nick Pivetta, Shane Bieber, Nick Martinez, Tyler Mahle, Foster Griffin, Michael Soroka

Relief pitcher
Emilio Pagan signs with Tigers
Pagan, 35, saved 57 games for the Cincinnati Reds over the past two seasons, although his 2025 numbers were rather ordinary (3.38 ERA, 25.9% K rate). Still, this is a franchise that desired Kenley Jansen and let him save 22 games last season even though there were better pitchers in the bullpen. Pagan produced nearly identical stats to Jansen. In other words, Pagan isn't so valuable -- but if all you care about are saves in a roto format, a healthy Pagan should provide at least 25 of them. -- Karabell (11/13)

Evan Phillips signs with Braves
Phillips, 32, posted a 2.36 ERA over parts of six seasons for the Los Angeles Dodgers. He also accrued 42 combined saves during 2023 and 2024. He missed most of 2025 dealing with Tommy John surgery and returned last season to pitch 26 effective innings. Additionally, Phillips has never permitted a run over 18⅓ postseason innings. The Braves figure to turn to Robert Suarez to close (because Raisel Iglesias is a free agent), but a healthy Phillips should accrue ample holds as well as occasional saves. -- Karabell (11/13)

Other free agents: Raisel Iglesias, Pete Fairbanks, Carlos Estevez, A.J. Minter, Blake Treinen, Martin Perez, Gregory Soto, Kenley Jansen, Hiromi Itoh (posted)

stories.headline: Max Verstappen admits to 40-hour GTA VI spree as he won Las Vegas GP
stories.summary: Max Verstappen claims he had already clocked 40 hours of Grand Theft Auto VI before his brilliant Las Vegas Grand Prix win at the weekend.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen claims he had already clocked 40 hours of Grand Theft Auto VI before his brilliant Las Vegas Grand Prix win at the weekend.

Verstappen delivered a masterclass of how to race with F1's new engines to win in Sin City, a race which saw an incredible 35 lead changes, but has since revealed that much of his downtime was spent binging through Rockstar's highly-anticipated new game, which came out on Nov. 19.

Revealing the total gameplay time to teammates on the Twitch channel of his esports team, Verstappen Sim Racing, formerly known as Team Redline, he was then asked if his flight home felt like the quickest ever because of the game.

"No, I was sleeping on the plane," he replied. "I played a lot in the evening and the morning in Vegas."

The release of the game coincided with the start of the on-track schedule in Vegas.

Verstappen was one of the drivers who admitted during media day on Wednesday that he had already pre-downloaded the game ready to play, which came out at midnight leading into Thursday.

The schedule followed with two practice sessions on Nov. 19, then qualifying and the race at 8 p.m. local time on Nov. 20 and 21 respectively.

When one of his fellow Twitch streamers quipped it was time well spent, he added: "Yeah! It's not like I can go out anyway."

Verstappen later revealed he does not watch any of the cut scenes around the game's story.

"I'm over 80% of the missions," he added.

- Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc 'unmanageable' - Ferrari boss

- Lewis Hamilton: I could have beaten Kimi Antonelli if I was Ferrari No. 1

- Haas confirm Rafa Camara will finish 2026 season with the team

The admission will add another layer to what will likely go down as one of the best and most memorable grand prix performances of his storied career, which also included a brutal putdown of Mercedes rival George Russell, who he claimed is "so far below my level" that he was unfazed by criticism the British driver had made earlier in the week.

Verstappen is known for gaming at all hours during F1 weekends.

In 2024, Red Bull's then-racing advisor Helmut Marko had to ask the Dutchman to stop streaming himself playing late-night sim racing sessions with Team Redline in the middle of the night and early hours of the morning during F1 weekends.

Verstappen later said the yo-yo Vegas race was something he had only ever experienced playing Mario Kart before.
